Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Issue #⁠245596 reports the Shoper cookie-consent dialog on www⁠.4motos.pl ("Dbamy o Twoją prywatność") plus its dark page mask; the reporter profile reproduced both. issue.title: www.eneba.com
issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder

### What product do you use?
Other ad blocker: AdBlocker Ultimate on Firefox, whose Ultimate Privacy Filter carries the same rule. The rule comes from the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, so AdGuard users are affected the same way.

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website doesn't work properly: Eneba's partner referral cookie is removed, so purchases are not credited to the partner who sent the buyer.

### Description
The generic rule `$cookie=af_id` in the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter removes the first-party cookie `af_id` on www.eneba.com.

Eneba's affiliate links carry `?af_id=<partner>`. When the page loads, Eneba's own script sets `af_id=<partner>` on www.eneba.com for 30 days, and that cookie is what credits the partner when the buyer checks out. If the cookie is removed, the referral is lost. Nothing cross-site is involved: it is Eneba's own cookie on its own domain.

The rule sits right next to `$cookie=afUserId`, so it looks aimed at AppsFlyer's cookies. On eneba.com the same name is used for something else.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Without the filter, open https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder
2. The page sets the cookie `af_id=keyfinder` on www.eneba.com, expiring in 30 days.
3. With the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter on, `$cookie=af_id` removes that cookie, so Eneba has nothing to credit at checkout.

A real case: on 26 Oct 2026 a buyer on Firefox with AdBlocker Ultimate clicked our link at 18:17 UTC and ordered at 18:18 UTC. Eneba did not credit the referral. Our other Eneba referrals from browsers without this rule are credited normally.

### Suggested fix
```
@@||eneba.com^$cookie=af_id
```

### Disclosure
We run keyfinder.gg, a game key price comparison site, and we are an Eneba affiliate, so this affects us directly. It also affects every creator and site in Eneba's partner program whose audience uses AdGuard or AdBlocker Ultimate.

issue.title: www.eneba.com
issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder

### What product do you use?
Other ad blocker: AdBlocker Ultimate on Firefox, whose Ultimate Privacy Filter carries the same rule. The rule comes from the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, so AdGuard users are affected the same way.

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website doesn't work properly: Eneba's partner referral cookie is removed, so purchases are not credited to the partner who sent the buyer.

### Description
The generic rule `$cookie=af_id` in the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter removes the first-party cookie `af_id` on www.eneba.com.

Eneba's affiliate links carry `?af_id=<partner>`. When the page loads, Eneba's own script sets `af_id=<partner>` on www.eneba.com for 30 days, and that cookie is what credits the partner when the buyer checks out. If the cookie is removed, the referral is lost. Nothing cross-site is involved: it is Eneba's own cookie on its own domain.

The rule sits right next to `$cookie=afUserId`, so it looks aimed at AppsFlyer's cookies. On eneba.com the same name is used for something else.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Without the filter, open https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder
2. The page sets the cookie `af_id=keyfinder` on www.eneba.com, expiring in 30 days.
3. With the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter on, `$cookie=af_id` removes that cookie, so Eneba has nothing to credit at checkout.

A real case: on 26 Oct 2026 a buyer on Firefox with AdBlocker Ultimate clicked our link at 18:17 UTC and ordered at 18:18 UTC. Eneba did not credit the referral. Our other Eneba referrals from browsers without this rule are credited normally.

### Suggested fix
```
@@||eneba.com^$cookie=af_id
```

### Disclosure
We run keyfinder.gg, a game key price comparison site, and we are an Eneba affiliate, so this affects us directly. It also affects every creator and site in Eneba's partner program whose audience uses AdGuard or AdBlocker Ultimate.

Indeterminate — On the reported Eneba URL the alleged breakage does not reproduce:⁠ with AdGuard Tracking Protection active the page renders intact, the affiliate referral is still captured (the 302 rewrites ?af_id= into utm_medium/utm_source and the site stores it in localStorage), eneba.com's other first-party cookies survive, and no af_id cookie was ever observed — even in the experiment phase where no rule applied.
